question_text: Find the equation of locus of a point the difference of whose distances from (−5,0) and (5,0) is 8 units.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what you would do with the modulus, and name the shape the locus turns out to be.

steps.label: Take the locus point
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own. Both fixed points lie on the x-axis, symmetric about the origin — the y-terms will cancel later because of it.
steps.memory_tip: Both fixed points lie on the x-axis, symmetric about the origin — that is why the y-terms cancel.
lines: Let P = (x, y) be a point on the locus.

recall.must_convey: That the moving point is named P = (x, y) and the fixed points are written down.

take the locus point as P x y
P equals x comma y is on the locus

name the moving point P with coordinates x and y

steps.why: Every locus question starts the same way: the moving point gets coordinates, and the condition is then written in terms of those coordinates.
common_mistakes: Giving the moving point fixed numbers instead of (x, y).
Mixing up which points are fixed and which one moves.

steps.label: Write the given condition
steps.margin_note: First mark. A modulus means the difference may be taken either way round, so the ± is carried from here on. It disappears at the final squaring, which is why the answer is still one curve.
steps.memory_tip: A modulus means either order, so carry the ± from here. It disappears at the final squaring.

recall.must_convey: That the modulus is opened as ±8, one distance is isolated, and squaring gives ±16PB = 64 + PB² − PA².
accept: open the mod as plus or minus eight then isolate one distance and square
P A minus P B is plus or minus eight so P A equals plus or minus eight plus P B
carry the plus or minus and square both sides
mod ni plus or minus ga open chesi square cheyyali
rearrange to get plus or minus sixteen P B on one side

steps.why: A difference of distances behaves like a sum: it cannot be squared in one go. Isolating one distance first is the same move, and the ± must be carried because the modulus allows either order.
common_mistakes: Dropping the modulus and writing only PA − PB = 8.
Squaring PA − PB = 8 directly and being left with a cross term.

steps.label: Substitute the distances
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both fixed points have y = 0, so the y² terms are identical and cancel outright, leaving a difference of two squares in x. Dividing by 4 keeps the numbers small.
steps.memory_tip: The y² terms are identical and cancel, leaving a difference of two squares in x.

recall.must_convey: That the y² terms cancel and the difference of squares in x gives ±4PB = 16 − 5x.
accept: the y squared terms cancel and the x difference of squares gives minus four a b
substitute and use a minus b whole squared minus a plus b whole squared equals minus four a b
both y terms are the same so they cancel leaving plus or minus four P B equals sixteen minus five x
y terms cancel avuthaayi, x lo difference of squares
reduce it to four P B equals sixteen minus five x

steps.why: Both fixed points sit on the x-axis at ±a, so the y² terms are identical and cancel, and what is left is a difference of two squares in x.
common_mistakes: Expanding both x-brackets fully and losing a sign instead of cancelling.

steps.label: Simplify to the locus
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. Squaring kills the ±, which is why a two-way condition still gives one curve. The x² and y² signs come out OPPOSITE — a hyperbola.
steps.memory_tip: Squaring kills the ±, which is why a two-way condition still gives ONE curve — a hyperbola.

recall.must_convey: That squaring again gives 9x² − 16y² = 144, a hyperbola.
accept: square again and collect to get nine x squared minus sixteen y squared equals one forty four
the minus one sixty x cancels and twenty five x squared minus sixteen x squared is nine x squared
square both sides once more and simplify to the hyperbola
malli square chesthe nine x square minus sixteen y square equals one forty four
the locus is a hyperbola

steps.why: A constant difference of distances to two fixed points is a hyperbola with those points as foci, so OPPOSITE signs on x² and y² are the expected finish — the one family here that is not a circle or an ellipse.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that −160x appears on both sides and cancels.
Writing 9x² + 16y² = 144 and turning a hyperbola into an ellipse.
